    Who offered $1 billion for a perfect bracket?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    Warren Buffett offered $1 billion to any of his Berkshire Hathaway employees who could fill out a perfect NCAA March Madness bracket in 2014, though the rules were later modified and the prize eventually shifted to smaller amounts, with a $1 million winner in 2025 for predicting 30 of the first 32 games. 
    The Original $1 Billion Offer (2014)
    • Who: Warren Buffett, CEO of Berkshire Hathaway. 
    • What: $1 billion to any Berkshire Hathaway employee who could predict all 67 games in the NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament. 
    • Why: The odds of achieving a perfect bracket are astronomically low (around 1 in 9.2 quintillion), making it a safe bet for Buffett. 
    Evolution of the Contest
    • Modified Rules:
      Over time, Buffett loosened the requirements, offering $1 million for predicting the first 48 games or later, $1 million for picking 30 of the first 32 first-round games. 
    • First Winner:
      In 2025, a participant finally met the revised criteria, winning the $1 million prize.

      Who is favored to win March Madness?
      An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
      AI Overview
      As of mid-March 2026, Michigan and Duke are generally considered the top favorites to win March Madness, often followed by Arizona and the defending champion Florida Gators, though odds shift as the tournament approaches; other strong contenders include UConn, Houston, and Illinois, with Duke recently emerging as the outright favorite according to some sources. 
      Top Favorites (as of March 13-14, 2026):
      • Michigan:
        Frequently listed as the overall favorite or a co-favorite by sportsbooks like BetMGM and FanDuel. 
      • Duke:
        Also a top contender, often second to Michigan or emerging as the favorite as conference tournaments begin, notes FOX Sports and USA Today. 
      • Arizona:
        Consistently ranked in the top three favorites alongside Michigan and Duke. 
      • Florida:
        The reigning champions remain a strong contender, often just behind the top three. 
      Other Strong Contenders: 
      • UConn: A strong program with recent championship history.
      • Houston: Known for strong defense and talent.
      • Illinois: Another team in the top tier of contenders.
      Where to Check Current Odds:
      For the most up-to-date favorites, check sports betting sites like BetMGM, FanDuel, and sports analysis sites like USA Today and FOX Sports.

        "Selection Sunday," the annual day of intrigue, angst and controversy for college basketball fans, looms this weekend. And it's shaping up as a big one for those rooting for the most popular programs in the region — Missouri, St. Louis University and Illinois.⁠ ⁠ How interesting could things be at 5 p.m. Sunday, when the NCAA Tournament bracket is unveiled in a one-hour program on CBS (KMOV, Channel 4 locally)? Each of those teams could end up in the field, which would be just the third time in this century that all three all would be participating at the same time, after happening in 2013 and 2000.⁠ ⁠ There's also a sidelight. For the first time in a decade NCAA tourney games will be played in St. Louis, on Friday and Sunday of next weekend.
